sections.topic_sentence: Do not memorize this vocabulary.
The ideas the whole argument turns on — the two theses, the conversion that grows the environment, the governing metaphor, and the vocabulary of models underneath them.
What a fleet of coding agents is, and the ways it comes apart.
The environment that holds the fleet to a standard, and the mechanisms it is built from.
MAGE's contribution is not a list of practices.
This book began with one hard engineering problem, watched closely over months of building a real production system.
Large software systems have always exceeded what any one engineer can keep in mind.

sections.heading_text: Why I built a production system to study this
sections.topic_sentence: This book began with DocAble, a production service for remediating inaccessible documents.

MAGE rests first on a single longitudinal case: one production system, built by one engineer using one vendor's agent ecosystem over several months and used in production by me and my colleagues at Purdue.

sections.heading_text: What the method turned out to be
sections.topic_sentence: Two theses organize MAGE.
This book is for software engineers who suspect the ground has moved and want to know where to stand.

sections.heading_text: What this book is about (and what it is not)
sections.topic_sentence: If you opened a book about agentic software engineering expecting a tour of agents, you may be surprised by what comes first.

points.text: Agent capabilities matter but are not the engineering object this book stabilizes; the durable problem begins when an agent works autonomously where "it usually works" is not an acceptable standard.

sections.topic_sentence: Think of a 3D printer.

points.text: The 3D printer is the book's governing metaphor.
When realization is cheap, leverage moves to the description.

sections.topic_sentence: Everyone can sketch a piece of software.

points.text: Anyone can picture software, but a picture will not print.
A printer needs a structural model plus print notes.
A picture yields a plausible instance, not a specification of what must hold.

sections.topic_sentence: Suspect the engineered setup before you infer a machine limit.

points.text: Suspect the engineered setup before inferring a machine limit.

Capable models execute a bad direction at speed; velocity is neutral — it amplifies sound and bad engineering alike — so abundant implementation increases the value of getting the upstream engineering right.

preamble_points.text: Coding agents make implementation cheap enough to change the engineering problem; a sound spec, a coherent model, and evidence do not arrive with that capacity — implementation speed amplifies whatever engineering surrounds it.
Treat the agent first as a printer, not the engineer of the whole system; when a build is wrong, inspect the engineered setup before inferring a fixed limit in the machine.

This is the Preface's question from the engineer's seat: as implementation becomes abundant, engineering leverage moves toward the instructions, representations, constraints, evidence, and infrastructure that shape autonomous work.

sections.topic_sentence: The explicit problem is a mountain of inaccessible documents.

points.text: The explicit problem: inaccessible university documents at scale.
One project answered both problems at once.

sections.topic_sentence: From the outside the system is almost boring, by design.

points.text: A user uploads a document; a checked file and its evidence return.

sections.topic_sentence: Building DocAble well is not one problem.

points.text: Building DocAble well is not one problem; different questions want different pictures.
Structure, behavior, policy, measurement, and provenance are five questions, each wanting its own reduction.

No one picture is the model of DocAble; each is a purposeful reduction that makes one question's facts cheap to see — comprehensiveness is not the goal; choosing the reduction the question demands is the skill.

sections.topic_sentence: To follow those questions you need a handful of names that stay put.

points.text: A handful of plain names that stay put across every later chapter.
A worker is one thing in the system and five things to an engineer, depending on the question.

sections.topic_sentence: Why hang a whole book on one system?

points.text: One example, opened as far as the question needs, teaches more than a shallow survey.

Parts II/III meet DocAble held still: Part II asks which representations make its properties tractable, Part III how selected obligations acquire authority; Part V tells how it came to be and what broke.
Enough of DocAble for now; the landmarks and the governed system are in place — before deciding what representations or controls it needs, inspect the productive substrate doing the work.

preamble_points.text: You will meet DocAble in every chapter; here is just enough to hold it.

sections.topic_sentence: The substrate is two parts, not one.

points.text: A foundation model and an agentic harness together form the engineering substrate; the useful unit is the pair operating inside an engineering environment.
The foundation model brings four properties.
The harness adds four properties of its own.

None of these properties is alien to human engineering; what changes is their combination and economics, and the harness-engineering literature reaches the same unit of analysis — the model-harness-environment system.

sections.topic_sentence: Scale creates a reasoning problem before an agent ever enters the picture.

points.text: Scale creates the reasoning problem before an agent enters; a long task is a campaign whose reasoning state grows while the active state available to the reasoner stays finite.
Once the task outruns active state, some state must live elsewhere and be reconstructed; poor reconstruction re-solves solved questions and contradicts earlier constraints — one source of churn.
Better models move the boundary by using available state more effectively; they do not abolish the locality problem — a better model searches the warehouse better but still has a warehouse.

Practice at codebase scale reports the same effect; the point is not a line-count threshold but that raw implementation is an expensive reasoning substrate when the question depends on a much smaller set of relationships.

sections.heading_text: The horizon is a locality problem
sections.topic_sentence: It is tempting to read this as a fact about today's context window, and so as a fact that the next model will erase.

points.text: Context windows are today's most visible instantiation of the limit, not the limit itself; the durable constraint is locality.
Software has always been arranged around the memory, compute, and communication hierarchy of its machine; agentic reasoning inherits the same obligation.
The reasoning horizon is the latest instance of a recurring software-engineering problem: the abstraction is organized around the physical limits of the machine.
A longer window or new architecture moves the wall without removing it; the hardware account earns that claim rather than asserting it.

sections.topic_sentence: The second problem is not that agents make mistakes while human programmers do not.

points.text: Software engineering has always separated authorship from assurance — we compile instead of trusting a prediction, test instead of accepting an explanation — because the producer's confidence is not enough.

Commodity intelligence makes that separation more important because implementation is cheap and repeatable; another judgment from the same substrate does not create authority — something outside the producing run must decide what evidence counts.

Some obligations need little modeling — a sandbox, compiler, test, or permission system holds them; those are real Alignment, limited by semantic reach. Modeling moves that boundary outward, making larger properties available to the reasoner and to deterministic machinery.

sections.topic_sentence: One property of the harness makes external authority practical.

points.text: Agentic work occurs in an observable loop; the engineer need not control hidden reasoning to govern what enters the system — authority can act at the seams the work has to cross.

Seams already support local controls without a system model; the deeper opportunity comes when the environment holds explicit abstractions of what matters — the harness supplies the control points, representation determines how much they can know.

preamble_points.text: Engineering methods fit the substrate they act on; agentic engineering begins by asking what productive substrate entered the process, because its combination and economics change what the engineering environment can do.

sections.topic_sentence: A broad reasoner can operate on abstractions, but its active reasoning state is finite and large systems contain far more detail than any one engineering question needs.

points.text: Problem A, representation: how should a large evolving system be represented so a finite reasoner works coherently over the properties that matter without reconstructing them from implementation?

sections.topic_sentence: Autonomous work can be locally constrained and checked without a comprehensive model, but probabilistic implementation cannot be its own final authority, and richer system-level obligations require semantics the environment must obtain somewhere.

points.text: Problem B, authority: autonomous work can be locally constrained and checked without a comprehensive model, but probabilistic implementation cannot be its own final authority, and richer obligations need semantics the environment must obtain somewhere.

sections.topic_sentence: The two problems are related but neither is reducible to the other.

points.text: The two problems are related but neither reducible to the other; MAGE teaches Modeling first as a methodological choice, not because Alignment is impossible without it — local controls can already be authoritative, but better abstractions enlarge what can be stated, reasoned over, and checked without recurring human reconstruction. Commodity intelligence removes implementation, not the decisions.

preamble_points.text: Commodity intelligence changes the economics of implementation without abolishing scale, uncertainty, and assurance; the substrate makes two old problems especially consequential — representation for a finite reasoner, and authority outside the producing run.

sections.topic_sentence: Modern agent architectures already externalize knowledge.

points.text: Agent architectures already externalize knowledge; a knowledge graph serves as an external reasoning substrate.
MAGE begins from the same observation, then asks what additional work a representation can do; shape does not distinguish the artifacts, semantics do.
A knowledge graph exposes what exists; an engineering model carries the semantics an engineering question needs. Authority is a separate dimension.

sections.topic_sentence: The simplest useful form for that knowledge is a graph — the *system knowledge graph*.

points.text: The simplest useful form of that knowledge is a graph.
Graph names the structure, not the storage technology.
Context engineering expressed structurally: relevance follows relationships.

sections.topic_sentence: Externalizing knowledge this way is the most basic move of the Modeling Thesis, and much of current practice already stands on it.

points.text: Externalized knowledge representation is the most basic move of the Modeling Thesis, and most of industry already stands on it.
Knowledge representation is universal in the corpus; graph-shaped representation common; invariant-bearing models not.

preamble_points.text: A foundation model knows the languages and patterns; it does not know your system — those facts live in the engineering environment.
Reconstruction from raw artifacts is possible; cost and scale are the problem — past the point where the reasoner can keep the state active, the next agent pays it again.
The first modeling move is modest: externalize engineering knowledge that should not have to be rediscovered.
The Modeling Thesis in its weakest form: externalize engineering knowledge into a compact world to reason through; this chapter earns only the first step.
Engineering compares alternatives through representations that suppress irrelevant detail; commodity intelligence increases the return on making the representation explicit and machine-readable.

sections.topic_sentence: Naming these capabilities gives the rest of the Part a useful ordering.

points.text: The capability ladder orders representational capabilities, not organizations; each step makes additional engineering questions answerable.
Read the ladder as a capability ladder, not a maturity model; authority is a separate axis — Docker shows real authority low on the ladder.

sections.heading_text: Richer models expose richer authority surfaces
sections.topic_sentence: Better representation pays first in reasoning.

points.text: Better representation pays first in reasoning — a service edge becomes a typed relation, a status string a transition, an ownership convention an explicit relation.

Once an obligation is explicit enough to evaluate, an Alignment mechanism can consume it. Modeling does not create authority by itself, and authority does not require Modeling; Modeling expands the semantic surface over which authority can operate.
Representation–Alignment Proposition: as engineering intent becomes more explicit and structured, more obligations become eligible for deterministic enforcement.

The practical consequence is not "model everything"; notice where a fact is repeatedly reconstructed or a property repeatedly adjudicated that the environment could settle if the right abstraction existed.

sections.topic_sentence: The ladder answers a question every real team asks: where do I start?

points.text: Start at the lowest step that solves a real reasoning problem; strengthen the model when a recurring question justifies it.

preamble_points.text: An edge gains representational capabilities one property at a time: type, semantics + obligation, derivation. Authority is related but separate.
Those are representational capabilities. Authority is related but separate — Modeling changes what the environment can KNOW explicitly; Alignment decides what it will DO with an obligation.

An engineering model is a deliberately reduced, machine-readable representation structured to answer an engineering question; MAGE favors models that can be queried, derived, traced, or checked so a trusted representation is not an unchecked second truth.

sections.heading_text: Why models are cheaper to keep alive
sections.topic_sentence: Models are not newly useful.

points.text: Models are not newly useful; commodity intelligence changes part of their maintenance economics — the repetitive upkeep a coding fleet performs cheaply and often.
The design cost remains — someone still decides which question deserves a model; what became cheaper is the repeated upkeep, which makes repository-native models practical.
Part V reports a controlled navigation pilot measuring one consequence of this design: reduced reconstruction cost.

sections.heading_text: The shared machinery beneath the views
sections.topic_sentence: Most of the catalogue's method models belong to no single view.

points.text: Shared machinery makes every view executable and drift-proof.

sections.heading_text: Derive and join; do not repeat
sections.topic_sentence: A model here is **derived** — from the code, or the code from it — never kept beside the code as a parallel document.

points.text: A model is derived and joined, never repeated.

sections.topic_sentence: A model and the code stay equal by derivation, and derivation runs in one of two directions.

points.text: Name the direction of derivation up front.
Most models are model-from-code; the codebase came first.

sections.heading_text: Separate observed fact from authored intent
sections.topic_sentence: Repository-graph tools demonstrate the descriptive half of the pattern: parse source into a persistent graph so an agent can traverse dependencies and identities without repeatedly rereading files.

points.text: Repository-graph tools show the descriptive half; extraction alone says only what IS. Deciding what is permitted, what a component ought to own, or which invariant to preserve requires authored intent.
The extracted graph supplies the IS; the authored model supplies the OUGHT; a check reads one against the other.
Prose specifications can carry an OUGHT too; their weakness is mechanical — prose is harder to compose, validate, and reconcile against a moving implementation.

sections.topic_sentence: A model earns trust over a claimed surface only if its elements can be related back to the system they represent.

points.text: A model earns trust over its claimed surface only if its elements relate back to the system; that relationship is traceability, and it should be live where practical.
Resolve the target against current code when the check runs; a deleted target then becomes a finding rather than a stale green edge.

sections.topic_sentence: Trust is bounded by the model's declared surface.

points.text: Trust is bounded by the model's declared surface; a model needs a credible relationship to the facts it claims, or every agent that treats it as a reasoning surface inherits the same stale assumption.
Two layers cover the relationship: a mechanical layer that re-derives or checks claims, and a judgment layer for semantics not yet captured by a predicate.

Two gaps remain: a semantic miss (the mechanical relation resolves but its meaning changed) and an unmodeled region (no relation to check). Both mark where human judgment is filling a representational gap.

sections.heading_text: An executable model is its schema plus its checked predicates
sections.topic_sentence: Operationally, an executable model is its structured schema plus the predicates and derivations machines can consume.

points.text: In the operational sense used here, an executable model is its structured schema plus the predicates and derivations machines can actually consume.
A structure that names its parts but carries no machine-consumable properties may still be a useful model; it is only half of the executable-model pattern this chapter builds.

sections.heading_text: How to read a model page
sections.topic_sentence: The appendix documents each model through a uniform five-field reference template: what the model is for, what it contains, how it is depicted, how its claims are checked, and how it stays tied to the code.

points.text: The appendix documents each model with the same five-field template.
An executable model is a structured representation plus checked claims.

preamble_points.text: An executable model participates directly in computation and can be mechanically reconciled with the system — an active engineering artifact, not a parallel description.
DocAble supplies the running examples; Part V gives the full system. Here we extract only the machinery that makes the teaching models trustworthy.
Every Part-2 model is one executable schema, worn several ways.

sections.topic_sentence: Draw those projections the classic way — several diagrams, each maintained on its own — and they drift independently, each ageing the first time its author forgets it.

points.text: Separate diagrams drift independently; projections over one connected substrate join on identity and expose contradictions.
Derivation, traceability, and parity checks keep a machine-readable view from becoming an unchecked second copy of the code.

sections.heading_text: The framework is a choice; the core is not
sections.topic_sentence: Framework and audience are separate choices.

points.text: Framework and audience are separate projection choices over one set of source models; a view may omit facts but never invent them.

sections.heading_text: The graph gives identity; the view gives semantics
sections.topic_sentence: The connected graph supplies identity and relationships; it does not supply every model's semantics.

points.text: Identity is shared across views; each view supplies its own semantics.

sections.topic_sentence: The models ahead sort by the kind of question each answers — five **classes**: structural, behavioral, decision, measurement, and documentation.

points.text: The models ahead sort into five classes by the kind of question each answers — the one coordinate system to carry forward.
The class tag names the question a model answers; the chapter groups models by the question you arrived with.

preamble_points.text: Each projection answers one engineering question; the model classes name the kinds worth projecting for.

points.text: The service-flow model answers what the system is made of and what depends on what.
One service graph generates the access policy and reconciles the real call graph.

sections.heading_text: Who owns each piece, and what may cross a boundary

points.text: The component-zone model makes ownership and boundary a queried fact.
Ownership and boundary reaches become findings, not slow erosion.

sections.topic_sentence: The component and zone model is the cleanest place to see a distinction that runs through every model in this book.

points.text: Descriptive facts are derivable; intent-bearing facts are authored.

sections.heading_text: The facts every consumer joins to
What third-party material the build depends on

preamble_points.text: Structural and decision models turn architecture, ownership, and boundaries into queryable facts.

sections.topic_sentence: The models below share a small formal vocabulary.

points.text: Behavior invariants are predicates over reachable executions; a state machine, two property shapes, and a bounded checker express them.
A remediation job's lifecycle — its states, legal transitions, and terminal states — is the chapter's representative behavioral model.
The transition table makes an illegal move unreachable in code, and terminal states have no edge back into processing.
The claim transition is won by exactly one worker, which sets up ownership as the next specialization.
A behavioral model makes the lifecycle a first-class object: states as an enum, transitions as a table, one guarded function the single writer.
The discrete job-lifecycle state machine is the behavioral model the surveyed industrial corpus rarely records.

sections.heading_text: Ownership over the lifecycle, a specialization
sections.topic_sentence: The state machine says what states a job may occupy.

points.text: Job ownership specializes the behavioral and structural views — an owner and a lease over the job lifecycle and the queue structures — and is not a sixth class.
Two workers doing the same chunk twice, and a dead owner losing work, are the two failures ownership must answer.
Ownership of a chunk rests on a lease plus a compare-and-set claim.
The lease provides crash recovery; the durable compare-and-set provides at-most-once effect. Recovery is not permission.
Broker redelivery after a lapsed lease is not the application's requeue path; the app requeue stays reserved for planned preemption, and timeout/crash surface as failed.
Represent single ownership explicitly and put an atomic claim under the lease; trust the claim for correctness, the lease for liveness.
Distributed locks and idempotency keys are the same shape; the surveyed corpus rarely governs it as a checked model.

sections.heading_text: What must hold across every interleaving
sections.topic_sentence: *What runs at once, and what stays true across every schedule?* Concurrency is where a correct-in-isolation design becomes a source of races, deadlocks, and torn writes, and the answer cannot be a thought experiment about interleavings.

points.text: Concurrency is where correct-in-isolation designs break; the answer is a declared, checked contract, not a thought experiment about interleavings.

sections.topic_sentence: *Where does each part run, and which of those placements is a correctness decision?* A functionally correct system can still be mis-deployed.

points.text: The deployment-topology model declares where each service runs, and parity holds it to reality.

sections.heading_text: Correctness in the graph, resource limits in a profile
sections.topic_sentence: The placement models raise one more question — *what resources constrain execution?* — and answering it well turns on a single modeling principle, the most portable idea in this chapter: **correctness dependencies stay in the graph; host-specific resource limits live in a scheduler profile.**

points.text: Correctness dependencies stay in the graph; host-specific resource limits live in a scheduler profile.

sections.topic_sentence: The policy models the load-and-cost side of execution, but not request latency, cache-hit ratios, or data-movement cost.

points.text: Model only where a failure lives; the load-and-cost model is built and the latency slice is left unmodeled by design, and Part V reconstructs the incident that exposed its cost.
These models make execution explicit — legal states, ownership, interleavings, placement, host-dependent resource policy — and hand off the evidence questions to the next chapter.

preamble_points.text: The structural models hold the system still; this chapter puts time, order, ownership, and place back.
Four engineering questions this chapter answers; measurement waits for the next chapter.

sections.heading_text: What the system promises about time and cost
sections.topic_sentence: Behavior says what the system does when it runs.

points.text: Measurement asks a question the scheduler does not — is the running system inside the throughput, latency, and cost bounds it promised?
The operational envelope is a small set of measured quantities, each paired with the ceiling it may not cross.
Instrumentation senses the measured quantities; an admission gate refuses work that would breach a bound before it starts.
The cost model is fully measured, yet production only reports the budget — the hard cost cap lives in an offline harness, not the live path.
Model the operational envelope wherever a breached bound must stop the system rather than let it degrade.
Operational-envelope measurement asks if the running system is inside its bounds; drift measurement asks if a model still matches reality.

sections.heading_text: Keeping the explanation true to the change
sections.topic_sentence: Documentation is easy to dismiss as prose about the real system.

points.text: Documentation stops being prose about the system and becomes evidence the moment the system changes a user's artifact.
Documentation is a model of the action; like any model it can drift, so derive it from a record the actor writes as it acts.
Measurement tells the system whether its quantitative promises hold; provenance whether its account is faithful; each answers one question in isolation, and the final chapter joins them.

preamble_points.text: Behavior models state what executions are legal; measurement and evidence models state what the running system promises and what record it must leave behind.

sections.topic_sentence: The user-journey model makes the product's journeys first-class typed entities — each an actor pursuing a goal through ordered steps, every boundary-crossing step joined to the endpoint it calls.

points.text: The user-journey model copies nothing; the other models join to it.

sections.topic_sentence: Three small models feed the flagship, each answering one question about a journey's tests.

points.text: A journey's criticality derives its test tier, never stored.
Projecting coverage onto nodes makes an untested invariant visible.
Task-closure types what the terminal assertion must mean.

sections.topic_sentence: Follow one fact — a journey is *major* — through four models without storing it twice.

points.text: Four models join on one fact, nothing said twice.

sections.heading_text: The three questions the join answers
sections.topic_sentence: Three questions the raw deploy scripts and test config cannot answer on their own.
[ref:join-composite] shows the four-model composition left to right.
The join's invariants span all four models, collected in [ref:scenarios-invariants].

sections.heading_text: The Selector and Scheduler in code
sections.topic_sentence: Two pieces of real policy code make the join concrete — the **Selector** derives a host's test roster from the journey model, and the **Scheduler** rations that roster per host.

sections.heading_text: Tracing one fact through four models
sections.topic_sentence: The join keys chain, and a reader can walk them against the figure: the **endpoint** ties M13 to M5, the **criticality** ties M13 to M6, the **derived tier** ties M6 to M7's roster, and the **host profile** ties the roster to the plan.

points.text: Four chained join keys round-trip major to serialized.

sections.heading_text: The Payoff Is in the Join
The models pay off when they join
sections.topic_sentence: Each model earns its keep separately.

points.text: The models are useful apart; their real value appears when they join.

sections.heading_text: A request walks the connected slice
sections.topic_sentence: Trace a single request.

points.text: One engineering question traverses the models along a single connected slice.

sections.heading_text: The graph is what lets the projections meet
sections.topic_sentence: The walk works only because every model names the same entities.

points.text: The system knowledge graph joins the projections on stable identity, not on hand-kept consistency.

sections.topic_sentence: A relation that lives only in human memory can still influence engineering work — a reviewer can remember it, an agent can infer it, a test may indirectly expose its violation.

points.text: A relation in memory can still influence work; Modeling supplies the stable semantic object, and Alignment decides what authority acts on it.
Once relations are explicit, more obligations become mechanically expressible; making the semantics explicit is the Modeling move, deciding what authority acts is the Alignment move.

MAGE teaches Modeling first not because Alignment is impossible without it — Docker's sandboxes disprove that — but because explicit abstractions move the boundary of what the environment can analyze and enforce.
The selection rule is unchanged — choose the coarsest representation at which the engineering question becomes answerable.

sections.topic_sentence: The models in Part II form a reusable toolbox organized by engineering question.

points.text: The mental toolbox is the Part's carry-away: a model, a property, a quality per concern.
The scenario is the join you perform across the six models, not a seventh model the system stores.

sections.topic_sentence: Some of these properties already have concrete mechanisms in DocAble; others do not.

points.text: Some modeled properties already have mechanisms and some do not; a model can make a property explicit and measurable before the organization decides a violation should block work.
Part III takes that variation as its subject — which obligations become constraints, which need sensors, which a validator judges, where a gate blocks, and where human judgment stays appropriate.

sections.heading_text: When Lightweight Models Stop Being Enough
sections.topic_sentence: MAGE does not replace established modeling disciplines.

points.text: This chapter is the doorway outward.
Graduate tools when the quality goal sharpens into a measurable constraint.
Each model is deliberately lightweight; a heavier method waits.
Model at the coarsest level that answers the question; descend only when it forces you to.

sections.topic_sentence: Can Alignment exist without explicit models?

points.text: Alignment can exist without explicit models — a sandbox, a compiler, a test, a reviewer are real authority; their limit is what the environment can state and observe without reconstructing semantics.
Local controls work on local facts; richer engineering questions often require a representation at the level where the property exists, or an agent fills the semantic gap each time.

Models change the scale of the questions we can reason about and the properties we can make explicit; as representation gets richer, more judgment becomes eligible for analysis and enforcement, and what stays outside stays probabilistic or human.

Part II ends where Part III begins: the models are not waiting to become real through enforcement — they already pay in reasoning, prediction, composition, and traceability — and Part III asks the separate question of authority.

preamble_points.text: A scenario walks a goal across several models joined on stable identities; its value is compositional, not a replacement for validating each model.
A user journey anchors the scenario; models enter where used.

sections.topic_sentence: The first boundary is **reasoning input** — the context, representations, examples, and instructions put in front of the reasoner.

points.text: The first boundary is reasoning input: ordinarily guidance, not authority.
The second boundary is the action: one attempted side effect the harness can inspect or refuse.
The third boundary is the work unit: a meaningful unit of many actions, where whole-work obligations become legible.
The fourth boundary is the artifact or runtime: forbidden state made impossible to express or accept.

sections.heading_text: Placement and strength are different decisions
sections.topic_sentence: The four boundaries do not form a monotonic scale from weak to strong.

points.text: The four boundaries do not form a monotonic weak-to-strong scale.
Guidance belongs on the map but not on the same axis; this is why substantial Alignment can exist with little modeling.

sections.heading_text: Every boundary is a place to close the loop
sections.topic_sentence: The boundaries also decide where feedback can return.

points.text: Every boundary also determines where feedback can return; earlier evidence means less to reconstruct.
These mechanisms do not act independently; the interplay is its own problem, deferred to §3.5.

The Alignment Thesis, stated whole: give engineering intent authority by encoding obligations into authoritative mechanisms — constrain, sense, evaluate, admit — which can act directly, models enlarging their reach.
Authority installed at a boundary is easiest to see in systems already running it.

preamble_points.text: The environment intervenes between a proposed action and its consequence.
Guidance influences behavior; authority constrains consequences.
Feedback is the third piece: it closes the loop without creating authority.
Agents are steerable; their outputs are not guaranteed by the instruction that steers them.
Security practice draws the same boundary: secure the process that produces the artifact.
Authority can act at several boundaries; choose where the obligation is visible and a mechanism can affect the consequence.

sections.topic_sentence: A drift check can establish a declared correspondence between two artifacts.

points.text: A drift check establishes agreement between two artifacts, not that the correspondence expresses the right intent.
The distinction is not derived versus authored; it is description versus independent obligation.
Drift checking has a precise job: preserve the correspondence the model claims to maintain; correctness needs another claim.

sections.topic_sentence: The second failure is placement.

points.text: An obligation can be perfectly stated and still be unenforceable at the boundary where you try to check it.
Checking model drift at the commit is the wrong granularity; the property belongs to the completed unit of work.
The design rule: place authority at the earliest boundary where the obligation is both legible and enforceable.
The rhyme: Modeling chooses the coarsest representation where the question is answerable; Alignment chooses the earliest boundary where the obligation is legible.
Real boundaries are sometimes approximate: semantic placement is an engineering trade-off, not a demand for a theoretically perfect hook.
The chapter has supplied both requirements for authority; the next question is what the mechanism at that boundary actually does.

preamble_points.text: Authority needs an obligation independent of the work being judged, and a boundary at which that obligation is legible.
An obligation may live in a model, or directly in a type, permission, schema, test, or policy; Alignment does not care which.
Those requirements produce two lessons: agreement is not correctness, and placement follows semantics.

sections.topic_sentence: Inside the loop a mechanism has one of two moves — prevent the mistake, or observe it — and [ref:constraint-vs-sensor] draws the split.

points.text: A mechanism is one of two moves: prevent, or observe.
A soft instruction becomes Alignment only when the environment can act on it.
A sensor observes and produces evidence — actual = observe(system); it does not judge, and acting on it costs an iteration.
A CI suite bundles sensor, validator, and gate without collapsing the distinction among them.
A sensor is only as good as its observability — the semantic gap from the other side.
A constraint prevents drift within the iteration, costing none.
Constraint and sensor echo control engineering — analogy, not identity.
Human process instantiates the same roles: logging senses, the reviewer validates, the approver gates.
The constraint is poka-yoke; jidoka is closer to a sensor/validator/gate bundle.
Ownership shows the pair at its sharpest: the compare-and-set is a pure constraint, the stale-sweep a pure sensor.

sections.topic_sentence: The other two roles act at the loop's closing door.

points.text: A validator turns evidence into a judgment.
A gate supplies the consequence — and a gate is a commitment.
Cheap evidence early, full re-derivation late; the thing asking to pass does not define passing.

sections.heading_text: The four roles, across the models
sections.topic_sentence: The service-flow model shows the complete loop.

points.text: The service-flow model runs the complete loop: a typed seam constrains, a scan senses, a diff validates, a gate blocks.
Other models emphasize different subsets of the four roles.

sections.topic_sentence: Keep **policy**, **guidance**, and **governance mechanism** separate.

points.text: Keep policy, guidance, and governance mechanism separate; authority begins when something acts.
The same artifact can play several roles; the model is the representation, the machinery the authority.
Implementations bundle roles; name them, don't stretch the terms.
Leave-with: intent becomes authority through one of four roles; next, where the mechanisms come from.

preamble_points.text: Four roles — constrain, sense, validate, gate — separate prevention, observation, judgment, admission.
Two roles act on the work; two act at the door it must pass.

sections.heading_text: Ex ante: encode what you already know
sections.topic_sentence: Start with obligations you can state before the work begins and whose recurrence justifies making them durable.

points.text: Ex ante: encode the obligations you can state up front, and stop paying judgment for them.

sections.heading_text: Ex post: convert what the work teaches
sections.topic_sentence: The harder half begins when the system surprises you.

points.text: Ex post: diagnose what was missing; not every failure wants another gate.
The conversion lands in one of five places: model, invariant, sensor, validator, or authority.
Modeling and Alignment form a feedback loop in practice without one being a prerequisite for the other.

sections.topic_sentence: Governance conversion gives software engineering something it has long had difficulty naming: a concrete form of **engineering capital**.

points.text: Governance conversion forms engineering capital — the concrete positive stock software engineering has lacked a name for.
The asset is not "the team learned" — it is something you can point at.
Capital earns a return: lower marginal engineering cost. Conversion is capital formation.
Capital depreciates; maintenance, reconciliation, and retirement manage it, so accumulation cannot be the objective.
Technical debt and engineering capital are symmetric stocks — both accumulate, both change the economics of later change, both compound.

sections.topic_sentence: Not every quality goal should end in a deterministic gate.

points.text: Where a goal lands turns on three questions; the first is whether the obligation is explicit in a form the environment can use.
The residual is an obligation nobody made explicit enough for the environment to use.
An explicit obligation may still resist cheap mechanical evaluation — an honest boundary, not failed Alignment.
Observed only: explicit and evaluated, yet un-gated — because a gate is a commitment.
A governed obligation carries an authoritative consequence appropriate to its risk; the four states are a design space, not a ladder.
The point is not to drive every obligation to the rightmost leaf; it is to know where each sits and why — and conversion has now created an estate to govern.

preamble_points.text: A governed environment grows ex ante and ex post; governance conversion is the hinge.

sections.topic_sentence: Start with the nodes.

points.text: Catalogue each control: a stable identity, the boundary it acts at, the resources it touches, the obligation it serves, and its authority role.
A catalogue alone cannot tell you whether two sensible controls conflict, nor whether an important obligation has no control; those are relational questions.

sections.topic_sentence: Two collisions from the case study make it concrete.

points.text: A collision lives between two controls, drawn nowhere until the graph draws it.
The interaction graph uses controls as nodes and shared resources as the principal join key; controls need not call one another to collide.
Shared resource is a useful conservative relation, not a proof that the graph captured every interaction.
Some candidate conflicts are mechanically decidable; others are semantic — a sensor produces evidence of the interaction, a validator or human judges whether it is a conflict.
A governed environment is a claim that its mechanisms compose; the graph makes that claim explicit and checkable at authoring time.

sections.topic_sentence: Interaction is only half of meta-governance.

points.text: A catalogue says what exists and a graph says where controls collide; neither says what should be governed but is not.
Coverage is a small requirements-traceability problem: an obligation with no adequate mechanism is under-governance; a mechanism with no obligation is an orphan.
A gap is under-governance; an orphan is governance debt. Neither is automatically bad — an orphan is a finding to reconcile, not proof to delete.

sections.topic_sentence: Governance conversion and coverage auditing pull in opposite directions, and a healthy environment needs both.

points.text: Governance conversion is reactive and coverage auditing is proactive; a healthy environment needs both.
The same audit pushes against permanent accumulation: engineering capital is not the number of controls.
The meta-model stays honest by symbol-anchoring: control entries are re-resolved to their implementations so the catalogue cannot retain controls that no longer exist.
Stop the recursion unless experience earns more: a governance model can itself become bureaucracy.

preamble_points.text: Every control can be reasonable in isolation and the system of controls still be wrong.
Successful environments accumulate machinery; that estate becomes an engineering object — a portfolio of capital assets to manage.
Alignment turned on itself: a model of the controls, made binding on the controls.

sections.topic_sentence: **Need.** A turn begins with something you want to learn, change, preserve, or make true.

points.text: A turn begins with a need, and honesty about where the uncertainty lives.
Model at the least unnecessary detail, not to reach the top of a ladder.
Exploration is an instrument of inquiry; delegability comes from the whole environment, not a model alone.
Align places authority at the earliest boundary that has the semantics to decide it, on evidence independent of the producer.
Convert the lesson when the future return justifies the upkeep.
Repeat: capital is formed, maintained, and retired — not merely accumulated.

sections.topic_sentence: Part III developed governance conversion in full.

points.text: When judgment repeats, ask what future work should inherit from it.
Conversion is capital formation, not mechanism accumulation.
The improvement loop has familiar ancestors; the changed condition is implementation abundance.

sections.topic_sentence: Keep one distinction sharp.

points.text: Guidance aims; authority binds consequences.
Do not make authority the automatic destination of every piece of guidance.
"Must never happen" is a signal, not proof; the mechanism follows the property, not the rhetoric.

sections.heading_text: Prefer structural prevention where the action space closes
sections.topic_sentence: Prefer structural prevention when the action space can honestly be closed.

points.text: Prefer structural prevention when the action space can honestly be closed; otherwise preserve the action space and add independent evidence.
The choice is not prevention-good-detection-bad; it is to place the strongest honest mechanism at the level where the property permits it.
DocAble used both sides at once: close the action space where it could, validate independently where a property was only legible after the change.

sections.heading_text: Size the work to the reasoning and the assurance
sections.topic_sentence: Not every agent task deserves the full apparatus of governed autonomy.

points.text: Not every task deserves the full apparatus of governed autonomy.
Two things shorten the leash: reasoning burden and assurance need.
Size work as transformations with explicit inputs, outputs, and checkable boundaries.
DocAble sizes the leap to bounded typed edits, so the unit of delegation lines up with a unit of evidence.
Task shape matters as much as task size; a well-sized transformation of the wrong shape still fails.

sections.heading_text: What the rest of this Part does
sections.topic_sentence: The chapters ahead run the method under different conditions.

points.text: The chapters ahead run the method under different conditions.
A short closing strips away DocAble and the named tools and leaves only the moves that port.

preamble_points.text: MAGE has three recurring moves: Model, Align, Convert.
The ordering is methodological, not a logical dependency.
Parts II and III supplied the vocabulary; Part IV supplies the operating rule.

sections.heading_text: Start with what you already have
sections.topic_sentence: Survey the estate before designing the replacement.

points.text: Survey the estate before designing the replacement.
Run two inventories in parallel: representations and authority.
Mature orgs often have much Alignment and weak system-level Modeling.
Treat the wiki you have as an informal model, not a knowledge graph.
The first improvement is connection, not replacement.

sections.topic_sentence: The migration runs in four stages, each a useful stopping point, so an organization does not have to reach executable models before the work starts paying for itself.

points.text: Four stages, each a useful stopping point.
The four stages compress to one operating line.

sections.heading_text: Know the destination, but migrate by useful slices
sections.topic_sentence: The near destination is a **trusted map** over the parts of the system that matter now: important claims have known anchors, important implementation regions have explanatory homes, and agents and engineers can navigate the join without rediscovering it from scratch.

points.text: The near destination is a trusted map over the parts that matter now.
The far destination is adequate representation and evidence for the quality case.

sections.heading_text: Migrate one bounded surface at a time
sections.topic_sentence: A live estate rarely tolerates a wholesale cutover.

points.text: Choose a bounded surface; let old and new coexist while the replacement earns trust.
Recover the representation top-down, bottom-up, or clean-and-induce.
A model-code disagreement has a three-way diagnosis: model, grain, or code.

sections.heading_text: Introduce new authority safely: Audit → Drain → Promote
sections.topic_sentence: A valid future invariant is not always a valid present admission rule.

points.text: A valid future invariant may not be a valid present admission rule.
Audit->Drain->Promote is an authority-migration pattern, not a Modeling->Alignment dependency.

sections.heading_text: Measure what the map still cannot explain
sections.topic_sentence: Model induction has a stopping problem: a representation can describe everything it knows without telling you what it omitted.

points.text: Model induction has a stopping problem; traceability run backward finds the edges.
Treat orphans as candidates, not automatic defects.
Use the omissions to choose the next modeling investment.

sections.topic_sentence: Recovering a model is only the first step.

points.text: Recovering a model is only the first step; the next question is what happens to the facts it owns.
A representation made authoritative in name while its contents are copied elsewhere decays into maintenance work the day after the copies are written.
The stronger rule: if a fact already has a queryable authority, consume or derive it rather than copying it.
Where two representations must remain independently authoritative, make their correspondence observable — and check it in both directions, because a one-way check lets the model lie.
Hidden substrate assumptions deserve the same treatment: represent the consequential ones strongly enough that the blast radius can be queried before the change.

sections.topic_sentence: A recurring gap does not automatically deserve machinery.

points.text: Price the expected future loss against the cost of building and carrying the response.
Draw cost against frequency and the sizing judgment gets a shape.
Price the upkeep — engineering capital depreciates and can be retired.
The estate was matured in place, not rewritten from a clean slate.

preamble_points.text: Most readers inherit an estate that is both liabilities and assets.
Two independent axes fix the starting move: existing system, settled intent.
The cells prescribe how a body of intent is represented and given authority, not project-wide governance.
Brownfield enters through two doors that converge fast.
The first estate induces and authors; the second recovers and reconciles.
Neither door scaffolds a complete governed environment before useful work.
Model-first and implementation-first are starting points suited to different conditions, not rival doctrines.
The practical question is not how much to model in the abstract but how much structure the next unit of work needs.
Implementation-first is heuristic search over the model's learned prior; it becomes churn when the search keeps rediscovering structure that should have been made explicit.

sections.topic_sentence: To validate a change is to assemble evidence that bears on its obligations and decide what consequence that evidence should have.

points.text: Validating a change means assembling evidence that bears on its obligations and deciding what consequence that evidence should have.
Never admit a consequential change solely on its author's word; generate falsifying evidence and place admission where the author cannot redefine success.
Independent evidence has several sources; no single kind of representation monopolizes validation.

sections.topic_sentence: An **oracle** is whatever supplies the judgment against which the observed result is evaluated.

points.text: An oracle is whatever supplies the judgment against which the observed result is evaluated.
Existing behavior can stand in for a surprising amount of written specification: a reference implementation supplies an executable oracle.
Explicit models supply oracles for properties no single example carries; modeling enlarges the semantic scale of the oracle without monopolizing the concept.
An example pins one point; a property states a law over a domain and lets a generator search a space.
A failing example invites a local repair; a broader property makes that repair easier to falsify if the class stays open.
The generative techniques share one loop and differ by generator and oracle; choose by the shape of the claim, not a maturity rung.

sections.topic_sentence: Let the engineering claim choose the search.

points.text: Let the engineering claim choose the search: a valid domain earns a property test, an untrusted boundary earns a fuzzer, a structured model supplies a richer oracle.
When a generated input exposes a defect, fix the stable obligation so the repair closes the class, not just the seed.
Reuse real producers before inventing a complete synthetic world; hand-build richer generation only when the claim earns it.

sections.topic_sentence: Coverage answers a question about a population.

points.text: Coverage answers a question about a population, so the population must exist before the percentage means anything.
Ordinary coverage starts from the code or the tests that already exist; it cannot see that an important behavior has no test at all if nothing first names that behavior as an obligation.
Explicit models can supply the missing census: transitions that need evidence, edges permitted or forbidden, failure paths, claims that must be discharged.
The distinction matters because coverage cannot see an obligation that was never instantiated.

sections.heading_text: Did the search cover the claim?
sections.topic_sentence: Generative validation adds an honesty question that a small example suite can often avoid: **did the campaign search the semantic region the claim is about?** Code coverage answers where execution went.

points.text: Generative validation adds an honesty question: did the campaign search the semantic region the claim is about?
Where traceability exists, follow each model claim to the code that realizes it and ask whether the campaign reached it; a high aggregate becomes a named gap.
Coverage remains evidence about the search, not proof of correctness; measure it where a missing region changes what you do next.

sections.heading_text: Give the verdict the right consequence
sections.topic_sentence: Part III separated four mechanism roles for a reason.

points.text: A sensor produces evidence, a validator evaluates it, a gate controls admission; one artifact can bundle roles, but they stay distinct.
Authority is a separate design decision from evidence quality; a validated verdict may report or may block.
Where a gate is appropriate, put it outside the producing agent's discretion and re-run the required evidence at the admission boundary.

sections.topic_sentence: Part III gave a placement rule for authority: **evaluate an obligation at the earliest boundary where it becomes legible and enforceable.** That catches a problem close to its cause.

points.text: Part III gave the placement rule for authority: evaluate an obligation at the earliest boundary where it becomes legible and enforceable.
Consequential work often deserves a second boundary: re-evaluate at the last safe point before the consequence becomes difficult to reverse.
The second check is not a substitute for the first and need not repeat every earlier check; re-run only the evidence whose freshness matters to admission.
That is why done is a claim, not a stored fact: at a consequential boundary, regenerate the evidence needed to justify the consequence.

sections.topic_sentence: None of these techniques is new.

points.text: None of these techniques is new; abundant implementation changed the relative price of implementation and inspection, not the algorithms.
The engineer does not disappear from validation; human judgment moves toward choosing obligations, designing representations, and calibrating validators.

sections.topic_sentence: Here is the move; one industrial team converged on it independently.

points.text: Placing the grader outside the author is a general move, not a DocAble idiosyncrasy.

preamble_points.text: Every engineering process must answer what evidence is sufficient to accept a change.
Validation begins with an obligation; an unsettled hypothesis has no mechanical truth to test.

sections.topic_sentence: Start with the healthy path of a recurring activity: how a bug moves from reported to fixed, how a feature moves from designed to shipped, how an agent moves from dispatched to landed.

points.text: A lifecycle: write the healthy path, then name the failure states that matter and the sanctioned recovery from each.
FMEA supplies a neighboring instinct — enumerate failure modes rather than inventing recovery under pressure.
Pair each prohibition with its sanctioned way out; a bare "don't" leaves a stuck agent with no exit.
The fleet's own lifecycle deserves the same treatment as the product: make its legal transitions explicit and validate the ones the environment can decide.
A report of "done" does not establish that the repository entered the required state; re-evaluate the entry condition at the work-unit boundary.

sections.topic_sentence: A lifecycle model says which states matter.

points.text: A lifecycle names the states that matter; binding a reaction to a transition makes the right procedure arrive at the right time.
Binding does not require a mechanical response: the firing can be deterministic while the payload still contains judgment.
Wire known failure events to sanctioned reactions rather than waiting for an operator to notice; the aim is to automate the arrival of the decision procedure, not every decision.

sections.topic_sentence: A good runbook does more than list commands.

points.text: A good runbook preserves how an experienced engineer reasons through a recurring situation, without pretending every step has one mechanical answer.
Conventional SRE runbooks externalize procedure; MAGE adds one distinction — type each step by who or what can honestly decide it.
A deterministic step should usually become executable: preserve the sanctioned operation itself, not a paragraph telling an agent how to reconstruct it.
A bounded-judgment step carries the material the judgment needs — relevant state, allowed choices, distinguishing criteria, required output — a prepared brief, not an instruction to "investigate."
An irreducible judgment should be surfaced honestly; the environment can collect evidence and narrow the question without pretending the final decision is mechanical.
Operational playbooks are models of engineering practice: they externalize not only what to do, but which kind of reasoning each step requires.
Determinizing a step buys a structured execution trace — evidence of what ran, not an explanation of why the decision was correct.
Type every step as runnable, delegable judgment, or human judgment, and let the type decide how the step is governed.
Systems that share no code reach for the same fence between the step a machine can decide and the step that needs a mind.

sections.topic_sentence: Operational control fails easily when it acts on a proxy that only sometimes tracks the property that matters.

points.text: Operational control fails easily when it acts on a proxy that only sometimes tracks the property of interest.
Observe and govern the state that actually constrains the system, not merely the state that is convenient to count.

Use the simplest direct signal available: govern memory pressure rather than job count, mediate a shared test resource rather than trust process isolation, record lifecycle state rather than reconstruct liveness from side effects.
This is not a demand for perfect observability; the point is to notice when a proxy drives a consequential decision and the approximation has stopped being good enough.
An operating loop needs evidence about its own state; the useful metric is the one that changes the next engineering decision.
Ousterhout's rule: measure one level deeper — one level, not arbitrarily deep — where the deeper cut exposes the decision the surface number hides.
A metric is evidence; a validator may interpret it against a bound and a gate may then act, but the number itself carries no authority.

sections.heading_text: One hard example: coverage measured one level deeper
sections.topic_sentence: Line coverage answers a **syntactic** question: did this line run under some test?

points.text: Line coverage answers a syntactic question — did this line run — not the semantic one an engineer has: is the claim this code makes exercised?
The fix joins a traceability graph to the ordinary coverage oracle: follow each model claim to its anchor and intersect its line range with the covered set.
The composition counts model claims and reports a named verdict — this invariant's code is exercised by no test — instead of an anonymous percentage.

sections.topic_sentence: Slide to the far end, where the metric stops being a number a threshold can act on.

points.text: A doc-derived test pins a doc-claim; its metric — is this doc-claim pinned? — is genuinely soft, with no machine-enumerable denominator.
Wire a soft signal to a blocking gate and you manufacture the hollow tests it was meant to prevent.
The detailed metric receipts — cold-start latency, the missing-model drain, the null-result ablation — are Part V evidence, not method.

sections.topic_sentence: An executable model earns more than documentation value when tools consume it directly.

points.text: An executable model earns more than documentation value when tools consume it directly — it becomes a reusable query surface for many consumers.
A component-distance grade read from the model supplies evidence to a validator, whose verdict determines the gate's behavior at this boundary.
Same finding, three gate behaviors, chosen by consulting the model — the grade is evidence read from the model, and the gate carries the authority.

sections.topic_sentence: Put the pieces together and operation becomes a recurring rhythm.

points.text: Operating MAGE is one recurring rhythm: the lifecycle names healthy progress and failure, events bind the reaction to the transition, the runbook gives each state a sanctioned next move, and metrics tell whether the loop is improving or merely busy.
The rhythm is still Model, Align, Convert, run day after day; maintain the resulting structure while it pays and retire it when it does not.
Run the rhythm long enough and the engineer's work becomes model design, governance design, and evidence engineering.

preamble_points.text: A method has to survive ordinary days, not only successful changes.
Operating MAGE makes recurring work explicit in four connected forms: lifecycles, events, runbooks, and metrics.

Not all operating structure is authoritative; a lifecycle is a model, an event fires deterministically though its payload may carry judgment, a metric is evidence, and authority appears only where a constraint, validator, or gate acts.

sections.topic_sentence: The three examples share a construction pattern, drawn in [ref:skill-recipe].

points.text: The three examples share one skeleton: base model, orthogonal models, a top-level procedure.
The skeleton matters more than the three shipped names.

sections.heading_text: Deliver the right context—and measure it
sections.topic_sentence: A reusable procedure helps only if the actor reaches it when it matters.

points.text: A reusable procedure helps only if the actor reaches it when it matters; packaging knowledge is not the same as delivering it.
The naive answer — load everything into standing context — merely moves the navigation problem inside the reasoner.
Keep standing context small enough that it can genuinely remain standing; retrieve richer slices according to the work.
Context has a cost: it consumes tokens, attention, and reasoning capacity, and stale guidance can actively misdirect work.
Treat context delivery as an engineering intervention and measure its effect: compare with and without, task success first, then diagnostics.
The model-based engineering pilot is one example of testing whether engineered context does what we claim, not the point itself.
Context delivery changes what the reasoner can see; it does not, by itself, change what the environment will permit — the bridge back to Part III.

sections.heading_text: Self-governance: apply the method to the agent's own work
sections.topic_sentence: Self-governance packages the method itself: **Modeling and Alignment turned on the agent's own engineering work.** It is not a third activity beside those two, and not a third thesis — it is the discipline of applying both to the work as it is produced.

points.text: Recurrence is evidence the environment may be missing something durable — not always a new control.
The skill carries a catalogue of mechanisms and a procedure for deciding which one fits.
Rules in boot context bind only where a mechanism gives them consequence.
A passive skill needs a hook to fire it; it resolves the classifiable cases and surfaces the design forks.
Governance is capital that can depreciate: watch for the teetering tower.

sections.topic_sentence: Self-operate packages the previous chapter's lifecycles, recovery paths, runbook step types, and operating heuristics.

points.text: Self-operate packages the previous chapter's lifecycles, recovery paths, and runbook step types.
The skill makes operating procedure repeatable; it does not replace the underlying tools or gates.

sections.topic_sentence: Self-communicate packages a different craft: engineer-facing prose and technical drawing.

points.text: Self-communicate packages a farther craft — prose and drawing — through the same skeleton.
The third skill is a boundary test for the architecture, not a third pillar of MAGE.

sections.topic_sentence: Reusable agent procedures are one concrete form of engineering capital, and the industry is finding the pattern in parallel.

preamble_points.text: A skill is one packaging form; a recurring procedure becomes engineering capital.
Packaging is not authority: prose is guidance, the surrounding machinery may bind.
Three shipped skills show one portable architecture, not three required MAGE parts.
Tool skill teaches an interface; mastery skill packages a decision procedure.

sections.heading_text: A real law, a real deadline
sections.topic_sentence: The Americans with Disabilities Act requires a public university to communicate with people who have disabilities as effectively as it communicates with everyone else.

points.text: Title II now governs a university's digital communication.
The 2024 DOJ rule made access part of the service.

sections.heading_text: What it costs to make one document accessible
sections.topic_sentence: The cost is easiest to see in one deck.

points.text: One real deck flags dozens of distinct accessibility issues.
Remediating a course by hand costs weeks of work.

sections.heading_text: Why a document is not just a file
sections.topic_sentence: Underneath the institutional bind sits a technical problem deeper than it looks — the reason this became a software project worth building rather than a policy memo worth writing.

points.text: A document is a visual and semantic artifact.
VLMs changed the feasible boundary; they did not make a production system.
The missing work was engineering around the model.
An uneven capability surface raised the structure the system owed.

preamble_points.text: The problem comes first; it sets the bar the system had to clear.
DocAble remediates documents toward standards universities must meet.

sections.topic_sentence: The project began in a committee meeting about the very deadline the last chapter described.

points.text: A bored meeting experiment recovered a slide's meaning.
The probe proved one component, not a system.
Students declined, so the project ran on an agent fleet.

sections.topic_sentence: The build moved through a recognizable sequence of stages — recognizable only afterward.

points.text: Each stage answered a concrete pressure.
The clean stages are a line drawn afterward.

sections.topic_sentence: The growing engineering environment is visible in one especially easy-to-count class of artifacts: project-specific lints and gate scripts.

points.text: The control count is evidence of investment, not quality.
The count measures investment, not capital or causal conversion.

sections.heading_text: The support ratio: the environment outgrew the product
sections.topic_sentence: Another coarse measure shows where the engineering effort accumulated.

points.text: Support apparatus outgrew the production code.
Three-to-one is a revealed investment, not a target.
Support code is capital only while future work inherits capacity from it.

sections.topic_sentence: The feature list is less revealing than where engineering judgment went.

points.text: The feature list is less revealing than where judgment went.
The environment grew larger than the product and absorbed the repeatable review burden.

preamble_points.text: The chapter establishes chronology and scale, not causation.
A fleet produced more code than any human could read.

sections.topic_sentence: A user uploads a file.

points.text: One upload crosses six product responsibilities and returns with standards findings, fidelity evidence, and provenance.
The larger engineering environment around the product path contains the models, tests, and machinery that made this degree of delegation possible.
DocAble narrowed document repair into a small action surface and used both sides of the Alignment Thesis.

sections.heading_text: The model as a bounded subroutine
sections.topic_sentence: DocAble uses frontier models where the task genuinely requires probabilistic interpretation, but it does not let that component own the workflow around itself.

points.text: Deterministic code decides when interpretation is needed, packages a bounded input, requires a typed output, and evaluates the candidate before incorporating it.
The model's answer is a candidate; the trust boundary is only as strong as the obligations the validator can actually evaluate, and semantic residuals remain probabilistic or human.
The analogy to proof checking is useful but limited: the validator is not a proof kernel; its value is that the producing component does not define success for itself.
The coding agents pose the same trust-boundary problem at a larger grain, but the full MAGE response adds more than typed I/O.

sections.heading_text: Some structure banked options; some was forced by failure
sections.topic_sentence: Not every consequential structure was born from failure.

points.text: Some consequential structure banked an option it was never built for; these are dividends of prior structure, not evidence every abstraction must be bought by an incident.
Other seams begin with a concrete failure and let us trace the response in layers; the finished boundary hides the sequence that produced it.
A convenient one-line call stripped the accessibility structure the product exists to add, and nothing caught it.

The response came in layers, and the sharpest was the enforcement itself mis-reporting green; the model stated the boundary, the API and check gave it authority, and the authority still had to be maintained.

A file path crossed a service boundary; a typed client made the mistake unrepresentable, and a human review found a bypass the tests missed — a boundary works only over the paths that actually cross it.

sections.topic_sentence: MAGE was not designed as a five-rung organization chart.

points.text: The five rung labels are retrospective names for the changing center of gravity of my own work, not a career ladder.

Alignment moved repeatable authority out of direct human review; Modeling moved system knowledge out of my head; human judgment moved toward the gaps the environment could not yet represent or decide.
Delegation climbed as far as the engineering environment could carry it; when representation or authority was too weak, the operator fell back into tactical work.
Direct human inspection carried everything; it failed as an operating model once generation outran review.
Evaluation was delegated before authority was; the audit's value was diagnostic, and its decidable findings revealed questions that no longer needed a language model.
Judgment was specialized and the decidable residue dropped into machinery; the probabilistic reviewers kept the questions the checks could not settle.
Representation made reasoning local; named zones externalized ownership so an agent could reason inside one region, and selected rules over the zone model received authority.
Explicit models carried system-level knowledge; declaration did not make them true, so model drift became its own failure class answered by traceability.
A later audit showed the incident was a class, not a one-off; mechanical correspondence checks retired a recurring class of stale-reference failure.
Forcing an engineering relation into an explicit representation creates new questions the environment can ask; in three cases those questions exposed shipping defects green tests had missed.
The staircase shows delegation increasing as the environment absorbed two kinds of work; human judgment moved toward strategy and residual semantics rather than vanishing.

sections.heading_text: Delegation climbed as far as the environment carried it
sections.topic_sentence: The project began with one human reading every line and ended with most implementation moving through an environment I primarily inspected through models, evidence, and exceptions.

points.text: The project began with one human reading every line and ended with most implementation moving through an environment inspected through models, evidence, and exceptions; no rung was planned.

Representation determines which larger questions no longer require reconstruction; authority determines which repeatable obligations no longer require human admission; human judgment fills the remaining gap.
Parts II–IV present the clean method; the case shows why those pieces exist and why they did not arrive as one package.

preamble_points.text: The Build gave chronology; this chapter asks what changed in the division of engineering labor, and reconstructs the delegation staircase.
A snapshot makes architecture look inevitable; the history shows which structures were designed, forced, or hardened, and what each let the engineer stop doing by hand.

sections.heading_text: The instruction satisfied to the letter
sections.topic_sentence: **Problem.** By April the system was 300,000 lines that worked but were janky.

points.text: An under-specified instruction is satisfied to the letter and voided in spirit.
"Use types" named a surface property, not the domain abstractions the types were meant to represent.
The retrofit combined a commodity-lint floor with a structured model per dense primitive region.
This was capital formation at brownfield scale — inherited abstractions, boundaries, and regression checks.

sections.topic_sentence: **Problem.** The service cost tens of dollars a day while idle on a Kubernetes cluster.

points.text: I optimized within an architecture that was itself the constraint.
A fix that keeps hitting the same wall is the signal to price a paradigm change.
A judgment becomes capital only when later work can inherit it — not every lesson in a head is capital.
